description: Composite three-panel figure characterising cryogenic-rolled (CR) Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C steel. (a) Stacked XRD profiles with x-axis 2θ (degree) from 30 to 100 and y-axis Intensity (a.u.); five vertically offset curves are labelled from bottom to top Underformed (black), CR 30% (red), CR 50% (blue), CR 70% (teal), CR 90% (magenta). Only austenite reflections are indexed — γ(111) near 43°, γ(200) near 50°, γ(220) near 73° and γ(311) near 90° — marked by dotted vertical guidelines; no martensite peaks appear in any pattern, and all peaks broaden progressively with rolling. (b) FWHM (°) of the austenitic (220) peak versus Deformation level (%) with printed square-marker values 0.496, 0.686, 0.776, 0.913 and 1.022, a near-linear monotonic rise. (c) Dual-axis plot versus deformation level: left axis ε/10⁻³ (black squares, "Microstrain") and right axis Dislocation density/10¹⁴ m⁻² (red triangles, "Dislocation density"), with printed values 2.8→7 for microstrain and 3.2→23.6 for dislocation density. Together the panels demonstrate that CR of this steel monotonically increases peak broadening, microstrain and dislocation density without any deformation-induced martensitic transformation.

subfigures.description: Stacked XRD patterns (2θ = 30–100°, Intensity a.u.) of the test steel for five conditions labelled Underformed, CR 30%, CR 50%, CR 70% and CR 90%. Only austenite reflections γ(111), γ(200), γ(220) and γ(311) are indexed (dotted guidelines); no martensite peak is visible and diffraction peaks broaden as deformation increases.

Line plot of FWHM (°) of the representative austenitic (220) peak versus Deformation level (%) with printed data labels 0.496, 0.686, 0.776, 0.913 and 1.022; the value rises monotonically and near-linearly with rolling deformation.

Dual-axis plot versus deformation level: left axis ε/10⁻³ with black-square 'Microstrain' curve (printed values 2.8, 3.6, 5.1, 6.2, 7), right axis Dislocation density/10¹⁴ m⁻² with red-triangle 'Dislocation density' curve (printed values 3.2, 6.2, 7.9, 12.9, 23.6). Both quantities increase monotonically, the dislocation density accelerating at high deformation.

observations.observation: Panel (a) contains five vertically stacked XRD patterns labelled, from bottom to top, 'Underformed', 'CR 30%', 'CR 50%', 'CR 70%' and 'CR 90%'.
Only four reflections are indexed in (a) — γ(111), γ(200), γ(220) and γ(311) — all belonging to austenite; no ferrite or martensite reflection is labelled in any of the five patterns.
The diffraction peaks in (a) broaden progressively from the bottom (Underformed) to the top (CR 90%) pattern, most clearly for the γ(220) reflection near 73° 2θ.
Panel (b) prints FWHM values of 0.496, 0.686, 0.776, 0.913 and 1.022 (degrees) against increasing deformation level, i.e. a monotonic near-linear increase of roughly a factor of two.

Panel (c) plots microstrain (black squares, left axis) and dislocation density (red triangles, right axis) on the same deformation-level abscissa, with printed microstrain values 2.8, 3.6, 5.1, 6.2 and 7 and printed dislocation-density values 3.2, 6.2, 7.9, 12.9 and 23.6.
In panel (c) the dislocation-density curve accelerates between the last two data points (printed 12.9 → 23.6 ×10¹⁴ m⁻²), whereas the microstrain curve rises more evenly.
The caption states that (a) shows XRD profiles of the test steel, (b) the FWHM of the representative austenitic (220) peak, and (c) the calculated microstrain and dislocation density.
The citing text states that a single-phase austenitic structure is observed in the undeformed test steel and that no deformation-induced martensitic transformation occurs throughout CR.
The citing text reports that the FWHM of the (220) plane increases from 0.496° in the pristine state to 1.022° after 90% CR deformation, matching the values printed in panel (b).
The citing text states that based on Williamson–Hall theory the microstrain rises from 2.8 × 10⁻³ in the undeformed state to 7 × 10⁻³ after 90% rolling, matching the black curve in panel (c).
The citing text states that the dislocation density of the test steel is 3.2 × 10¹⁴ m⁻² in the undeformed state and increases gradually with deformation (red curve, panel c).
The citing text gives the Williamson–Hall parameters used for the analysis: shape factor K = 0.9 and incident-beam wavelength λ = 0.15406 nm.

unreadable_items: panels (b) and (c): the deformation levels of the intermediate data points are not printed as x-axis tick labels; their positions are only estimated from the gridlines (visually corresponding to roughly 30%, 50%, 70% and 90%)
panel (a): no numeric scale is given on the Intensity (a.u.) axis and the individual curves are offset arbitrarily, so absolute intensities cannot be compared
